title: Continuous complex functions on compact Euclidean sets are integrable
statement: Use $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field] with Euclidean topology and Lebesgue measure. For every integer $m\geq1$, every compact subset $K\subseteq\mathbf R^m$, and every function $h:K\to\mathbf C$ continuous for the subspace topology, $h$ is Lebesgue integrable on $K$, and $$\int_K |h(x)|\,dx<\infty.$$ The assertion includes empty compact sets. One may identify $\mathbf C$ with $\mathbf R^2$, and $\mathbf R\times\mathbf R$ with $\mathbf R^2$, with their usual Lebesgue measures.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: X = R^m (also X = C or R x R), E = C, mu = volume, at lines 592–594. Extend h by zero outside K; ContinuousOn of this extension on K is exactly the stated continuity in the subspace topology. Euclidean volume is finite on compact sets; Euclidean spaces are Hausdorff and have Borel measurable opens, satisfying all surrounding hypotheses. IntegrableOn includes integrability of the norm. No continuity of the extension outside K is used.
